short_description: The ship navigates the Ghost Currents, using the sea's memories as camouflage to approach Vex's domain undetected.
weather: calm but unnatural, with glowing mist clinging to the water's surface

text_blocks.content: You nod to Quinn, pointing toward the densest concentration of mist. 'Take us through the memories. Let the sea hide us.'
'Aye, Captain. But we must move like a ghost ourselves. No sudden turns, no raised voices. The currents here... they listen.'

Quinn guides the ship with painstaking slowness into the thickest part of the glowing mist. As you enter, the world outside seems to dissolve. The water around the hull no longer looks like water at all, but like moving images, translucent and shifting.

[The ship glides silently through a panorama of fragmented sea-memories: a merchant vessel sinking in a storm, a pod of whales singing, a pirate duel on moonlit decks, all playing out in silent, glowing loops.]
The Ghost Currents don't just hide you—they absorb you. The sound of your own ship fades. The creak of the rigging is swallowed by the soft, sighing hum of the sea remembering itself.
This is power of a different kind. Not to command the waves, but to become part of their story. Is this what Vex learned? To not just rule the sea, but to merge with it?
[A low, melodic hum, like a chorus of drowned voices.]
Time loses meaning. It could be minutes or hours. The crimson glow of the Depths grows steadily brighter ahead, a bloody beacon in the spectral haze.
[A particularly vivid memory-flash surges against the port side: Vex's ship, the 'Siren's Call,' cutting through these same currents months ago, its sails billowing with unnatural wind.]
'Captain... look. The sea remembers his passage too.'

You watch the phantom ship in the mist. In the memory, Vex stands at the prow, the coral crown gleaming on his brow. He isn't fighting the currents. He's... reading them. His hand moves as if conducting the memories themselves.
The realization hits you like cold water. He's not just hiding in the memories. He's learned to navigate them. To use them as a map and a shield.
[The humming shifts, becoming more dissonant, anxious.]

The mist ahead thins abruptly. You've reached the edge of the Ghost Currents. Before you lies the mouth of the Crimson Depths in terrifying clarity. Vex's ship, the real one, is anchored at the heart of the swirling maelstrom, protected by a ring of sharp, pulsating coral.
[Vex's ship is wreathed in a faint, shimmering aura—a bubble of calm within the violent whirlpool. Figures move on its decks.]
'We're close enough to spit on his deck, and he hasn't raised an alarm. The memories hid us well. But we can't stay here. The currents are starting to... recognize we don't belong.'
Quinn is right. The mist around your ship is no longer passive. It presses closer, the faces within it turning to look at your vessel with hollow eyes. The sea's hospitality is wearing thin.
'We have the advantage of surprise. But only for a moment. Do we strike now from the mist, or do we wait, watch, and learn what he's truly doing down there?'
